chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Two men entered upon Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so he placed a pillow for each one of them. One of them sat upon it, but the other refused. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sit upon it, for no one refuses an honouring except for a donkey.'
Then he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When an honourable one of a people comes to you, so honour him.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.كَرِيمُ قَوْمٍ: an honourable/noble person of a people
key_terms.وِسَادَةً: a pillow (symbol of honour and comfort)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for receiving guests and how does the Imam explain refusing hospitality?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the virtue of *karam* (generosity) by accepting a guest's refusal of a pillow as a sign of humility, yet correcting the one who refused out of pride by comparing such stubbornness to a donkey. He reinforces this by citing the Prophet Muhammad’s directive to honour guests, highlighting the Shia emphasis on social etiquette and the reciprocal nature of respect between host and guest. This incident underscores the scholarly view that accepting honour is a form of gratitude, while refusing it without valid reason can be seen as arrogance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Two men came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> placed a pillow for each one of them, and one of them sat upon it and the other one refused. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sit upon it, for no one refuses an honouring except for a donkey’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When an honourable one of a people comes over to you, so honour him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Once two men came to Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) he prepared one seat for each one. One of them sat on the seat but the other refused. Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) said to him, ‘Take your seat; no one refuses to appreciate being honored except a donkey.’
The Imam then said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “When the honorable person of a people comes to you, you must treat him with honor.’”
